teams.heading: Jake White named Fiji head coach ahead of 2027 Rugby World Cup
teams.body: White was confirmed in October, and the 35-man group he has put together for the November block is the first real measure of his thinking. Fiji come into the Tests off a 34-28 win over Japan and face France, Ireland and Italy, with four uncapped players in the squad. The appointment is aimed at the 2027 World Cup, the bigger horizon beyond these matches.

lead.why: Team-specific coaching story that is not already in the reader's recent editions, and it frames the November block around Fiji's new head coach.

teams.heading: Dallaglio warns Borthwick England's penalty count must fall before Australia
teams.body: Lawrence Dallaglio splits England's penalty problem into pressure penalties, when they dominate the gainline, and execution penalties, when players pick the wrong option. He wants Steve Borthwick's side to show a noticeable difference, starting against Australia. The figures back his case: England have conceded 98 penalties in eight matches this year, an average of 12.25 a game, plus 14 yellow cards and one red. Against Argentina they gave away 15 penalties and four yellow cards, and still won 31-24.

lead.why: A former England captain's discipline warning ahead of the Australia test is a team-specific story, backed by concrete penalty and card figures.

teams.heading: France, third of 12 in the log, have won two of three
teams.body: The points difference sits at +41, built from a 116-75 scoring split across three matches. The latest result, a 42-15 win over Japan in Round 3, keeps France in a strong position. Fiji come next in Round 4, and the figures suggest the attack will be the main thing to watch when France meet them. Those margins matter in a table this close, where a single result can shift the standings.

teams.heading: Jimmy O'Brien back in full training ahead of Ireland's Argentina opener
teams.body: Jimmy O'Brien is back in full training with Ireland after clearing return-to-play protocols following the concussion he suffered in Leinster's win over Munster, a welcome boost before Friday's Nations Championship opener against Argentina at Aviva Stadium. Assistant coach Paul O'Connell said the squad has had "very few players on the sideline", a point he tied to the smaller group in camp. Ireland's Sunday statement confirmed the update ahead of next Wednesday's team selection announcement.

teams.heading: Domingo Miotti earns first Italy call-up for South Africa test
teams.body: Montpellier fly-half Domingo Miotti is in Gonzalo Quesada's 33-man squad for Saturday's test against South Africa in Turin. Eligible through his Italian family and clear under World Rugby's Regulation 8 after his last Argentina test on 9 July 2022, the Tucumán-born playmaker had said he would wait until July and would welcome consideration, the coach says. He was unavailable last week through injury but can now train normally.

teams.heading: Magnus Bradbury left out of Scotland squad as Ollie Leatherbarrow preferred
teams.body: BBC Sport's Andy Burke said on 30 October that he was shocked by the omission and did not see it coming, least of all Leatherbarrow being picked ahead of him. He had flagged Bradbury, who has been very good this season, as a chance for the eight jersey while Jack Dempsey is unavailable in the Six Nations. Burke suggests Bradbury's worst display of the season, against Toulon in the Challenge Cup, came at a bad time, calls him unlucky, and wonders what his future at Test level looks like.

teams.heading: Joe Hawkins says he has no regrets over missing the 2023 World Cup
teams.body: Joe Hawkins, ineligible under the 25-cap rule after swapping the Ospreys for Exeter in 2023, says he has no regrets about missing that tournament. "I have no regrets," he said, adding that it makes him even more excited about what lies ahead. Since returning with the Scarlets he has been Steve Tandy's go-to at 12, starting eight of the last 12 Tests, and he says club intensity rises in a World Cup year as players chase places.

teams.heading: Franco Molina misses out as Tomás Lavanini returns for Ireland clash
teams.body: Franco Molina, a mainstay of Felipe Contepomi's second-row selections since his 2024 debut, is not in the 33-man squad for the Ireland opener, the first November roster without him. Veteran Tomás Lavanini comes back in his place. Also omitted are veterans Matías Alemanno, Gonzalo Bertranou and Matías Moroni, the latter with 99 Test caps, while uncapped second-rower Luciano Asevedo, who has trained with the group this year, also misses out.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson slams Kurtley Beale's Wallabies recall after five years away
teams.body: Wilson's criticism came on Sky Sport NZ after Les Kiss named Beale in the squad for the November Nations Championship games. Wilson, a former All Blacks winger, said of the 95-capped playmaker: "I love Kurtley Beale as a guy but this is not moving forward, to me it is surprising." Kevin Putt agreed Beale could be an option at fly-half but said full-back would be a fantasy. For Australia, the question is whether experience can help build depth at 12 before next year's home World Cup.

teams.heading: Japan's new kick-catch plan is being countered by opponents, analysis argues
teams.body: The note.com analysis says Japan have used a new kick-catch method since the start of this year, with player B rather than player A making the catch. The writer says it reduces the risk of penalties for escorting, but the catcher must run backwards and gets support only from player A. The analysis says the method is now being countered, and suggests opponents could let Japan catch and then apply pressure, or drop kicks deeper. It says the issue was highlighted in the Fiji match.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson hails Peter Lakai as world's best openside flanker
teams.body: The verdict came on Sky Sport NZ's Breakdown show, where Wilson called the 23-year-old 'a generational athlete'. It rests on a Hurricanes campaign in which Lakai played a central role in the 2026 Super Rugby Pacific title, and on his featuring in all four Springbok Tests, starting the last two, before he wore the number seven jersey for the Bledisloe Cup matches. Wilson would pencil him into a teamsheet beside Jordie Barrett, and says the quiet loose forward will not celebrate himself.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus to name Springboks for Italy clash on Monday evening
teams.body: Six uncapped players in the November touring squad could earn their first Springbok caps in Turin, and SA Rugby has confirmed Erasmus will reveal the starting side on Monday evening South African time. The six are Yaqeen Ahmed, Sebastian de Klerk, Luan Giliomee, Markus Muller, Riley Norton and Emmanuel Tshituka. If Muller debuts, he would become the youngest Springbok in the professional era, breaking the record Frans Steyn set 20 years ago against Ireland.
